site.name: Barker No. 3
site.location: Boulder County Tungsten Mining District / Clark Tunnel area
overview: Barker No. 3 was a documented tungsten mine in Boulder County's historic tungsten district, developed through two surface shafts, adits, and a lower connection reached from the Clark Tunnel.

Colorado and U.S. Geological Survey records identify the property in the northeast quarter of Section 18, T1S R72W, and report production of at least about 6,000 units of tungsten concentrate during the district's active mining era.

timeline.text: Barker No. 3 was developed as part of the dense network of tungsten workings west of the former Tungsten settlement in Boulder County.
State and federal mine reports documented two upper shafts, an adit entering southwest of the shaft area, another caved adit, and a separate Clark Tunnel section with a drift and winze.
Colorado's Metal Mining Fund summarized Barker No. 3 as a former producer with recorded output of 6,000 tungsten units or more and cited USGS Professional Paper 245 as the principal mapped source.

moreHistory: Colorado's Tungsten Mines of Colorado places Barker No. 3 in NE1/4 Section 18, T1S R72W. It locates the shaft 1,175 feet southwest of the Vasco No. 6 shaft and records the Barker vein about 650 feet inside the Clark Tunnel.

The same state report describes two distinct working sections. The upper section included two shafts, an adit entering from southwest of the shaft, and another adit that was already caved when documented. The lower Clark Tunnel section consisted of about 110 feet of drift on the vein and a 25-foot winze.

USGS Professional Paper 245 includes a plan of the Barker No. 3 workings and geologic surface sketch. Remnant uses an approximate historic mine-level identification point derived from the documented Barker No. 3/Vasco No. 6 spatial relationship; it does not claim that an individual shaft collar or surviving opening has been field-surveyed or is safe or accessible today.
